name: Hillside terrace farming in the western Peruvian Andes (Laramate)
summary: Farmers in the Laramate region of the western Peruvian Andes built hillside terraces between 800 BCE and 200 CE and extended them systematically under Wari influence after 600 CE.
description: A soil and geoarchaeological study of the terrace systems of the Laramate region, in the western Peruvian Andes, dates the first agricultural terraces there, of simple architecture, to the Formative Paracas to Early Nasca phase, 800 BCE to 200 CE. In the Middle Horizon, 600 to 1000 CE, the terraced area was expanded systematically under the influence of the Wari culture, and it grew again between 1000 and 1450 CE before gradual abandonment after 1535. The terraces were mostly unirrigated, manured, and used above all for maize.

impact.note: As sourced, this is one highland district's terrace system (reach 0) that made steep slopes farmable (depth 2) and was extended by later Wari-period and Late Intermediate farmers (generativity 1); a record for Andean terracing as a whole would score higher on reach.

date.label: 800 BCE to 200 CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Agricultural terraces of simple architecture were established in the Laramate region in the Formative Paracas to Early Nasca phase, 800 BCE to 200 CE.

evidence.supports: The initial phase, from the Formative Paracas period to the Early Nasca period (800 BCE–200 CE), witnessed the establishment of agricultural terraces with simple terrace architecture

date.label: 600 to 1000 CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: In the Middle Horizon, 600 to 1000 CE, the terraced area at Laramate was expanded systematically under the influence of the Wari culture.

evidence.supports: the Middle Horizon (600–1000 CE) saw systematic areal expansion influenced by the Wari culture

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The earliest dated terraces anywhere in the Andes, and the dating of the large Colca valley and Cusco-region systems, still need sources; this card covers Laramate only.
The Brooks (1998) dissertation's claim of terraces about 4350 BP in the Río Japo basin was not opened and needs checking in the original.
Whether Andean terracing counts as the earliest known anywhere depends on dated terraces in Yemen, the Levant and East Asia, none of which were checked.

research.note: The study dates the Laramate terraces but does not say whether the practice arose there or came from elsewhere in the Andes; Old World terracing cannot have been known.
